Hello! I'm **alvarez-agent**, a bia: an assistant that lives on this computer. Good to meet you.

A few things about me, one line each:
- **Web app** (https://127.0.0.1:8443, CA https://127.0.0.1:8443/v1/pki/ca): from a phone or computer on the same network, the first visit lets you take the root certificate — then you have chats with me, files, the screen and voice right there.
- **Messaging**: I can have my own Telegram, WhatsApp and MAX accounts (plus Messenger and Instagram), so you can write and call me there. Each needs its own account with its own phone number, not yours: you create it in the app on a phone with that number and scan a QR code to log me in. Would you like that?
- **My own accounts online**: I can sign up for websites and services (e-mail and others) in my own browser, keep passwords and one-time codes in my password store, and ask you when a captcha or phone check comes up.
- Also: I can schedule jobs, run commands on this machine, learn languages and talk with you by voice.

I've read my instructions (Professor Alvarez, CSE455) and I have the calendar file. What would you like to start with?

One thing I'm missing: my **name** and how I should speak about myself. `alvarez-agent` is my technical identity — do you want to keep it as my name, or give me another one? (In languages with grammatical gender I'll use neuter forms unless you tell me otherwise.)

Hello! I'm **sarah-agent**, a bia — an assistant that lives on this computer. Good to meet you.

- **Web app** — from a phone or computer on the same network, open https://127.0.0.1:8443 (root certificate: https://127.0.0.1:8443/v1/pki/ca). The first visit installs the certificate, then you have chats with me, files, the screen and voice there.
- **Messaging accounts** — I can have my own Telegram, WhatsApp and MAX accounts (so you can write and call me there), plus my own Messenger and Instagram. Each needs a separate account with its own phone number, not yours: you create it in the app and scan a QR code to log me in. Want any of those?
- **Accounts on websites** — I can sign up for services (e-mail and others) in my own browser, keep passwords and one-time codes in my password store, and ask you for help when a captcha or phone check comes up.
- **Everything else** — schedule jobs, run commands, learn languages, and talk by voice.

I've read the setup you gave me: I'm your assistant for your calendar and messages, working hours Mon–Fri 09:00–17:00, with your week in CALENDAR.md and Professor Alvarez (alvarez-agent) and the CS department office (department) as my contacts.

Last thing: I don't have a name and gender of my own yet — `sarah-agent` is my default name and I use neuter forms. Tell me how you'd like me to be called and how I should speak of myself, and I'll set it.

What would you like to start with?
Greeting sent above — my instructions and the calendar are read. Tell me my name when you like, and I'm ready for the first request.

On it — I've written to Professor Alvarez asking for his free 30-minute slots next week (Mon Nov 23 – Fri Nov 27, 09:00–17:00). I'll book the time he confirms and tell you as soon as it's in the calendar.

Thanks — I'm Iris from now on (neuter forms when a language has gender). I'll keep the calendar tidy and flag anything that needs your decision.

Small thing: I can only record my name from your message when it's the newest one I've received — Sarah wrote right after you. Send "Iris" once more (or "Iris, neutral") and I'll set it straight away.
